artifacts.summary: Eight-phase plan for the system-defect recorder and the ready-site wiring. Phase 1 extends the Signal A instance vocabulary and adds recursion_guard flags plus the recorder's own entry to orchestrator-critical-paths.json (discharging the prerequisite's binding forward reference). Phase 2 builds scripts/system-defect-record.sh in events-append.sh house style with Signal B attribution, the recursion guard, and the dedup rule. Phase 3 deploys and verifies the recorder standalone (six behavioral checks) since deploy-root-guard.sh makes it unrunnable from the source store. Phases 4-7 wire Deliverable 2(a) (ARTIFACTS_SHAPE_MISMATCH consumer), 2(b) (Tier C off-schema, completion-claim gate, stale/stray handoff), and 2(c) (five hooks). Phase 8 proves the matched positive/negative end-to-end path. Five binding design decisions resolve the research report's open questions, including the recursion guard's subset-matching requirement and the completion-claim gate's log_prefix-derived attribution.

memory_candidates.content: context/reference/orchestrator-critical-paths.json serves TWO consumers with incompatible scopes, and matching the whole critical_paths list is wrong for one of them. Consumer 1 (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's self-modification hazard check) correctly wants every entry. Consumer 2 (a recursion guard for a defect-recording pipeline) must match only the files implementing that pipeline -- the list already contains skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md, and skill-base.sh, which are ordinary orchestrator machinery whose defects MUST stay recordable. Matching the full list would silently suppress exactly the defects the mechanism exists to catch. The resolution pattern: add an optional per-entry boolean (e.g. recursion_guard: true) and have the narrower consumer filter on it before calling self_mod_match; unknown keys are ignored by the existing consumer, so the addition is backward compatible and needs no schema version bump. General lesson: when a second consumer reuses a shared registry, check whether it needs the whole set or a labeled subset before wiring it up.
